recipe_version.title: Pork Shōgayaki: Japanese Ginger Pork with Shredded Cabbage
recipe_version.description: A Japanese weeknight staple: thin slices of pork loin seared in a hot pan with onion, then glazed in a punchy fresh-ginger, soy, and mirin sauce. Served with a cool pile of finely shredded cabbage and steamed rice.

ingredients.name: green cabbage
ingredients.preparation: very finely shredded and chilled in the refrigerator

ingredients.name: short-grain white rice
ingredients.preparation: rinsed until the rinse runs clear

steps.title: Start the rice and prep
steps.body: Combine the rinsed rice and 1 3/4 cups water in a 2-quart saucepan, bring to a boil, cover, cook on low 15 minutes, then rest covered; it cooks inside this prep and the searing (overlap stated). Shred the cabbage very fine and chill it. Slice the onion and scallions. Grate the ginger and stir it with the soy sauce, mirin, and sugar. Season the pork with the salt and dust lightly with the flour.

steps.title: Sear the pork
steps.body: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high. Lay in half the pork in a single layer and sear 1 minute per side until lightly browned. Move to a plate and repeat with the remaining oil and pork.

steps.title: Cook the onion
steps.body: Lower to medium and cook the onion in the same pan until soft and lightly browned, 4 minutes.

steps.title: Glaze
steps.body: Return the pork, pour in the ginger sauce, and toss for 2 to 3 minutes until it bubbles and reduces to a glossy glaze.

steps.title: Plate
steps.body: Pile the chilled cabbage on one side of each plate, lay the pork and onion beside it, spoon over the pan sauce, and add rice and scallions.

allergen_notes: Soy and wheat from the soy sauce; wheat also from the flour dusting.
